I will keep my system simple, intensive, and realistic for Quzhou County at the start of the season. I am in the North China Plain, so I will stay with the wheat-summer maize rotation on most of my land because it matches local temperature, irrigation conditions, machinery use, and market familiarity. At my age, I do not want a fragmented plan with too many specialty crops that increase labor peaks and management risk. Since my education level is high, I am comfortable using improved seed, balanced fertilization, and tighter field monitoring, so I will push for stable yield rather than gamble on niche crops. I will use improved winter wheat and hybrid summer maize, manage fertilizer in a balanced way instead of chasing nitrogen alone, and keep irrigation targeted because water matters. I will plough before wheat where I need residue incorporation and root-zone improvement, then use rotary tillage for maize after wheat harvest to save time. I will also keep a small peanut block in spring to diversify income and spread risk, but I will not let it dominate the farm because the wheat-maize system is still the backbone of what I trust here. I will use pesticides only as needed but, in planning terms, I assume a modest number of applications because disease, insects, and weeds are normal enough that I would budget for them.
